_note: Pins that deterministic code must never no-connect on the model's behalf.
This is policy, not net-name classification, so it lives in data rather
than in normalize.py: it is edited by whoever finds the next counterexample,
and each entry records why it is here.
It exists because auto-closing a pin makes it invisible to ERC. Measured:
an ESP32-C3 whose EN pin was closed reached pipeline.ok=True with zero
findings from self-ERC, compliance AND kicad-cli — a board held in reset
This list is necessarily incomplete. Every pin it does close is written to
run.json under auto_nc so a reviewer can see what it decided.
Supply and ground pins are NOT listed here: they are recognised by
netnames.is_supply_pin / is_ground_pin, which covers vendor suffixes.

never_auto_close.reason: enable and power-down straps — a floating EN holds the part in reset
never_auto_close.evidence: ESP32-C3 with EN closed: self-ERC 14->0, kicad ERC 15->0, pipeline.ok False->True

never_auto_close.reason: regulator feedback and compensation — the size threshold protects nothing here
never_auto_close.evidence: 17-pin TLV62095 FB(5)/EN(13)/SS(9)/PG(4) all closed; 82 Regulator_Switching symbols with an FB pin are >= 16 pins
USB-C CC pins are PASSIVE, so an electrical-type filter misses them

never_auto_close.reason: test and power-on-reset pins whose default state is not obvious
never_auto_close.evidence: documented-NC handling belongs to mark_documented_no_connects, not to a blanket close
